# Scientific Optimization Log: The Quest for 50 Tokens/Second

- **Model:** `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q6_K_MoE_Q4_0.gguf` (35.5B params, 256 experts, 4 active experts, 41 layers)
- **Target Generation Speed:** `≥ 50.0 tokens/second`
- **Quality Invariant:** 100% pass rate across the 6-suite verification harness (`comprehensive_quality_suite.py`)
- **Rule:** Exactly **one single change** per experiment, verified and logged meticulously.

### Run 1: N-Gram Speculative Decoding (n_max=5, ngram_size_n=8)
- **Hypothesis:** Repetitive token sequences (syntax, formatting, indentation, code structures) will be speculated with zero model weights overhead and verified in batches by the target model, increasing throughput without any degradation to accuracy.
- **Parameters Changed:** Added `--spec-type ngram-mod:n_max=5,ngram_size_n=8`.
- **Quality Score:** **6 / 6 (100% Passed)**
- **Generation Speed:** **`11.64 t/s`** (+2.8% speedup; peak 11.84 t/s on topological sort and logic puzzle).
- **Draft Acceptance Rate:** 50.0% – 68.6%.

---

### Run 2: Native Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) Speculative Decoding
- **Hypothesis:** The model has native MTP weights (`nextn.*`) embedded in the GGUF. Enabling them will predict the semantic next token on *every* decode step across all text types, dramatically beating n-gram matching.
- **Parameters Changed:** Added `--override-kv qwen35moe.nextn_predict_layers=int:1 --spec-type mtp:n_max=1`.
- **Quality Score:** **6 / 6 (100% Passed)**
- **Generation Speed:** **`14.58 t/s`** (+28.8% speedup; peak 14.93 t/s on math and 14.90 t/s on facts).
- **Draft Acceptance Rate:** **`89.7%`** (1,207 accepted out of 1,345 generated!).

### Approach A: Autoregressive Draft Model Speculation (Qwen3.5-0.8B)
- **Hypothesis:** Speculating candidate tokens with a tiny separate autoregressive draft model (`Qwen3.5-0.8B-Q4_K_M.gguf`, 532 MB) will generate drafts rapidly for batch verification on the 35B MoE target model.
- **Outcome & Findings:**
  - Drafter standalone throughput: `33.71 t/s` (evaluating on CPU).
  - Draft acceptance rate on reasoning: **`8.56%`** (37 accepted / 432 drafted at $n_{\text{draft}}=16$).
  - Target decode throughput: **`2.39 t/s`**.
  - **Memory Contention Law:** On a dual-socket CPU workstation, both target (24.6 GB) and drafter (532 MB) compete for the same physical memory channels and cache lines. When the drafter misses a token, all remaining draft tokens in the batch are discarded, starving target execution.
  - **Contrast:** The embedded **Native MTP Head** (Layer 40) executes within the existing weights buffer, achieves **`89.7%` acceptance**, and reaches **`21.02 t/s`**.
